name: Permanent Loans
headline: Long-Term Permanent Commercial Mortgage Financing
description: Permanent loans provide long-term, fixed-rate financing for stabilized commercial real estate assets. These loans typically feature 5 to 25-year terms with competitive rates from banks, life insurance companies, CMBS conduits, and agency lenders. Ideal for cash-flowing properties with stable occupancy, permanent financing locks in predictable debt service and maximizes long-term returns.
description_extended: As the most common form of commercial real estate financing, permanent loans serve as the backbone of investment strategy for owners seeking to hold and operate income-producing properties. Sources include traditional banks, credit unions, life insurance companies, CMBS lenders, and government-sponsored agencies like Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac for multifamily assets. Each source offers different advantages in terms of rate, leverage, flexibility, and prepayment structure.

name: Construction Loans
headline: Ground-Up Construction & Renovation Financing
description: Construction loans fund ground-up development and major renovation projects for commercial real estate. These short-term facilities typically feature 12 to 36-month terms with interest-only payments during the build period, funded through progressive draws as construction milestones are met. Lenders include banks, debt funds, and specialized construction lenders.
description_extended: Construction financing is inherently higher risk than permanent lending, which means lender selection and deal structuring are critical. Experienced borrowers with strong track records can access competitive bank construction loans, while more complex or speculative projects may require debt fund capital. Key considerations include loan-to-cost ratios, interest reserves, completion guarantees, and the exit strategy — whether that's a permanent loan take-out, sale, or refinance.

Sources include debt funds, private lenders, and select banks willing to provide transitional capital.

name: SBA Loans
headline: SBA 504 & 7(a) Loans for Owner-Occupied Properties
description: SBA loans offer below-market rates and high leverage for qualifying owner-occupied commercial properties. The SBA 504 program provides up to 90% financing with long-term fixed rates, while the 7(a) program offers flexible terms for business acquisitions, expansions, and working capital. These programs are specifically designed for small businesses that occupy at least 51% of the property.
description_extended: The U.S. Small Business Administration partners with banks and Certified Development Companies (CDCs) to provide guaranteed lending programs that reduce risk for lenders and increase access to capital for small business owners. The 504 program features a unique two-loan structure: a first mortgage from a bank (50% LTV) and a second position CDC/SBA loan (40% LTV), with only 10% borrower equity required. The 7(a) program provides a single-source loan with an SBA guarantee up to 85%.

name: Mezzanine & Preferred Equity
headline: Mezzanine Debt & Preferred Equity Financing
description: Mezzanine and preferred equity fill the gap between senior debt and common equity in the commercial real estate capital stack. These subordinate capital positions allow borrowers to increase total leverage beyond what senior lenders provide, reducing the equity required for acquisitions, developments, and recapitalizations.
description_extended: Mezzanine debt is secured by a pledge of ownership interest in the borrowing entity rather than a mortgage lien on the property, while preferred equity involves an actual equity investment with a preferred return. Both serve a similar function — increasing leverage and reducing sponsor equity requirements. These structures are commonly used for value-add acquisitions, development projects, and recapitalizations where senior lenders cap at 65-75% LTV.

name: DSCR Loans
headline: DSCR Loans for Real Estate Investors
description: DSCR loans qualify borrowers based on property cash flow rather than personal income, making them ideal for real estate investors who own multiple properties, operate through LLCs, or whose tax returns do not reflect their true investment income. Commercial Lending Solutions sources DSCR financing from a national network of non-QM lenders, debt funds, and private capital sources for multifamily, mixed-use, and commercial investor portfolios.
description_extended: Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) lending evaluates a property on one simple question: does the gross rental income cover the debt service? If the property cash flows, the loan qualifies. This structure eliminates the need for tax returns, W-2s, pay stubs, or traditional income documentation, making DSCR a powerful tool for high-net-worth investors, self-employed borrowers, and portfolio landlords scaling their holdings. Typical DSCR thresholds range from 1.10 to 1.25, meaning the property generates 10 to 25 percent more income than the loan payment. Lenders include dedicated non-QM platforms, balance-sheet debt funds, and select private lenders with appetite for investor residential and small commercial assets.

name: Hard Money Loans

description: Hard money loans provide asset-based, short-term financing for commercial real estate acquisitions, repositionings, and distressed property purchases where speed and flexibility matter more than rate. description_extended: Hard money lending is the fastest capital available in commercial real estate. Unlike bank or agency financing, hard money lenders focus almost entirely on the asset: the current value, the after-repair value (ARV), and the exit strategy. Borrower credit and income documentation requirements are minimal by design. This makes hard money ideal for auction purchases, foreclosure acquisitions, time-sensitive off-market deals, and properties that need work before qualifying for conventional financing. The tradeoff is higher rates and fees relative to institutional capital, which is why hard money is almost always used as a bridge to a permanent loan or sale. Commercial Lending Solutions matches each deal with the right private lender based on asset type, market, loan size, and timeline to ensure competitive terms even in this space.

name: Bridge-to-Perm Loans
headline: Bridge-to-Permanent Loans for CRE Acquisition and Stabilization
description: Bridge-to-perm loans combine a short-term acquisition or construction facility with a pre-committed permanent take-out under one lender, eliminating the refinance risk that comes with executing a separate take-out on a stabilized asset. Commercial Lending Solutions sources these structures from banks, debt funds with forward commitment programs, and agency lenders offering Forward Standby Commitments for multifamily.
description_extended: Traditional value-add or ground-up commercial real estate execution requires a sponsor to close a bridge or construction loan, complete the business plan, then refinance into permanent financing through a separate process. This exposes the sponsor to interest-rate risk during the construction or stabilization period and the execution risk of finding a permanent lender willing to underwrite on day-one stabilized fundamentals. A bridge-to-perm structure removes both. The bridge or construction phase prices and underwrites with the permanent take-out already in place, often at a locked rate or rate cap, and converts automatically upon meeting pre-agreed stabilization tests (DSCR, occupancy, NOI). This product is most powerful for ground-up multifamily that will convert to agency, value-add commercial that will convert to bank or life company, and large industrial developments with credit tenant pre-leases.

name: 1031 Exchange Bridge Loans
headline: Bridge Financing to Meet 1031 Exchange Deadlines
description: 1031 exchange bridge loans allow investors to close on replacement property within the IRS 45-day identification and 180-day closing deadlines without waiting for conventional financing. These short-term facilities close in 10 to 21 days, satisfying exchange timing requirements while a permanent loan is arranged post-close. Minimum deal size is $2 million, aligned with the equity profiles of investors doing tax-deferred exchanges in commercial real estate.
description_extended: A failed 1031 exchange triggers full capital gains tax recognition on the relinquished property sale, often representing hundreds of thousands of dollars in immediate tax liability. The primary risk is not finding the right replacement property — it is failing to close on one in time. Conventional bank financing is simply not fast enough for most exchange timelines, particularly when the identified property requires due diligence, PCNA reports, or appraisals that banks require before commitment. A 1031 bridge loan from a debt fund or private lender eliminates the timing risk: the investor closes the exchange, locks in the tax deferral, and then refinances into permanent debt at leisure. Experienced 1031 exchange advisors and qualified intermediaries routinely recommend bridge lenders to their clients for exactly this reason.

name: C-PACE Financing
headline: Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy (C-PACE) Financing
description: C-PACE (Commercial Property Assessed Clean Energy) financing provides long-term, fixed-rate capital for energy efficiency, renewable energy, and sustainability improvements to commercial real estate. Repaid as a property tax assessment, C-PACE does not require senior lender consent in most states and can be placed behind existing first mortgages, making it a powerful tool for reducing capital expenditure while meeting sustainability goals. Minimum project size is $500,000.
description_extended: C-PACE has become a mainstream component of the CRE capital stack as building owners face pressure from ESG requirements, utility cost reduction goals, and property renovation needs. Because C-PACE is structured as a property tax assessment rather than a loan, it repays through the property tax bill and transfers to the next owner at sale, eliminating personal guarantee requirements. Eligible improvements include HVAC systems, roofing and insulation, LED lighting, solar and battery storage, EV charging infrastructure, seismic retrofits, and water conservation systems. C-PACE providers operate in 38 or more states and the District of Columbia, with programs available for new construction, existing building retrofits, and ground-up development.

name: Owner-Occupied Commercial Loans
headline: Commercial Real Estate Loans for Business Owner-Operators
description: Owner-occupied commercial loans provide financing for businesses purchasing or refinancing the commercial property they operate from. Whether through SBA programs, conventional bank financing, or credit union balance-sheet loans, these facilities allow business owners to build equity in their operating real estate rather than paying rent. Commercial Lending Solutions sources owner-occupied financing for office, retail, industrial, medical, and mixed-use properties from $1 million and up.
description_extended: Owner-occupied commercial real estate financing is fundamentally different from investment property lending because the primary repayment source is the business itself, not property rental income. This means lenders evaluate global cash flow: the business earnings and personal income of the owner-operator, not just the property DSCR. SBA programs are the most popular execution for owner-occupied commercial because they allow up to 90 percent financing with below-market rates and long amortization. Conventional bank and credit union programs are the alternative for borrowers who exceed SBA size standards, have stronger financials, or need larger loan sizes than SBA maximum limits.
